items.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was working with Lee Fortier. He had lots of bands.

ctx.x: Whilst playing at Bill Bennett’s club, I think the day after New Year’s Eve in 1951, the two of you are married, and you then applied to LSU, and enrolled there as an English major, and you made Baton Rouge your base for the next number of years. It seems that your experience at LSU was crucial in forming your mature sensibility, crystallizing a lot of the different threads you’d been working with while perhaps not really thinking about it.
Yeah. Well, I was working with Lee Fortier. He had lots of bands.
You also worked a little club on weekends. Feets or something like that.
